recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless a future ballot explicitly asks to add a separate numeric FMM extension to normative terminology artifacts.
issue_request: FHIR-16009 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core request asking that ElementDefinition's required value sets, including resource-slicing-rules and the parallel discriminator-type, property-representation, resource-aggregation-mode, reference-version-rules, and constraint-severity value sets, not remain draft FMM 0 while ElementDefinition went normative.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites svn revision 14464. In git history, 44e6df5562160cf956ea56f34b6c8dcdb6655c10 is the matching git-svn commit, titled "GF#16009 - fix bug setting fmm levels etc for value sets used in data types", and it changed datatype validation/generation context so datatype-owned value sets inherited FMM and standards status.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini lists ElementDefinition as an active data type and marks it normative. Current source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml still declares the affected required bindings. Current build output marks all six named ValueSets and CodeSystems standards-status normative; R5 publication shows the six ValueSets as normative with FMM 5. R4 publication already marked them normative, though it retained an FMM 2 extension, so the current build has moved beyond the original draft-FMM problem.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the accepted issue was already applied and the current source/build surface is correct.
